leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members put the optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) as their sole preferred prize part, with the citation 'for the invention and development of the optical lattice clock'. They share the view that it is a single, well-defined invention, independently reproduced in Sr, Yb and Hg, with a two-name attribution that most call the cleanest on the list. They do not share a common reading of its distinctness from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize: all six record this as the main reservation, and several (Lindroth, Kroll, Johansson) judge it answered while Danielsson and Olsson leave it open. Danielsson and Olsson explicitly hold a different first-ranked discovery from their opening round (B056 Higgs and B009 aberration correction) and say so. Two further members, Eriksson (B035) and Mehlig (B022), list B008 as their first alternative. The chair is among the six supporters and has tried to state the counter-arguments at their full strength.

Eriksson alone prefers magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) as a prediction-plus-discovery pairing whose phases are reproduced by many groups. The member concedes that the pairing mechanism is unsettled, that Yuan Cao and other experimentalists lie outside the three names, and that the citation should be worded narrowly on the platform and phases. Mehlig and Olsson raise maturity or attribution concerns about B035, and Johansson cites the same concerns as reasons to prefer B008; Olsson lists B035 as an alternative. No other member prefers it.

Mehlig alone prefers trapped-ion quantum logic (Cirac, Zoller, Blatt) as an original, thirty-year, widely confirmed line from proposal to realisation. Mehlig concedes that the experimental share is contestable because Wineland's NIST group and Monroe also contributed and the 2012 prize covered part of the foundation. Johansson and Kroll rank B022 as an alternative, Johansson ranks it just behind B008, and Pearce and Kroll both press the Blatt allocation. Mehlig names B008 as the more compact and less disputed prize if those points are not resolved.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members' statements treat B008 as scientifically sound and mature; no member disputes the physics of magic-wavelength trapping, the roughly 1e-18 performance, or its independent reproduction in several laboratories.

The two-name Katori and Ye attribution is described by most members as cleaner than the three- or four-name allocations elsewhere on the shortlist, although Johansson, Danielsson, Lindroth and Olsson add that other groups (NIST, PTB, SYRTE, Tokyo) have claims outside the two names.
If any of B008, B035 or B009 is pursued, members broadly agree the citation must be drafted narrowly on the invention or platform itself and avoid claims about mechanism or downstream technology.
scientific_disputes: Weight of fundamental physics: Eriksson holds that B008 is mainly a large precision gain and does not change understanding of matter as a tunable correlated-electron platform does, while Pearce, Danielsson and Johansson point to relativistic geodesy, tests of varying constants and a new SI second as physics beyond engineering.

Distinctness from earlier prizes: whether the lattice clock is a separate invention or a refinement of the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize. Kroll, Lindroth and Johansson judge it distinct; Danielsson and Olsson regard it as contestable; Mehlig notes the same overlap argument also applies to B008 and weakens the case against B022.

Whether B009 is a fundamental-physics discovery or primarily an enabling instrument whose payoff lies in materials science and chemistry (Pearce, Eriksson) as opposed to a mature invention that underpins atomic-resolution work (Olsson, Eriksson as alternative).

Whether the B012 circuit QED discovery is distinct from the macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation recognised in 2025: Johansson, Eriksson and Mehlig hold the arguments are real but contestable.
attribution_disputes: B008: Katori for concept and first demonstration versus Ye for record accuracy and many-body operation is described as clean by Danielsson, Johansson and Pearce, but Lindroth, Olsson and Johansson note that early lattice-clock proposals and the NIST, PTB, SYRTE and Tokyo groups are not covered.
B022: the experimental half is contested between Blatt and Wineland's NIST group or Monroe, and Mehlig, Johansson, Kroll and Pearce all say the third laureate is a judgment call.
B035: Yuan Cao and other experimentalists (Fatemi, Dean, Young) are outside the three names, as Eriksson, Mehlig and Johansson note.
B009: Krivanek and independent STEM-corrector work complicate the Rose, Urban, Haider trio (Olsson, Eriksson, Pearce).
B056: the three-name limit forces an arbitrary choice among Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee, and Danielsson and Olsson proposed different three-person sets from the four credited names.
B012: Lindroth and Mehlig note Girvin and Huang as omitted names.
maturity_disputes: The pending redefinition of the SI second: Johansson and Pearce say it should not delay a B008 prize, while Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Mehlig list it as a timing question that cuts either way.

B035: the origin of superconductivity and the correlated states is still debated about seven to eight years after the experimental discovery; Eriksson argues a prize can precede mechanism, while Mehlig and Johansson prefer the question to settle further.
B022: scalable quantum computing has not yet been achieved, though Mehlig argues the criterion concerns the invention and not the final technology.
B042: Johansson and Pearce note that source identification for IceCube rests on a few associations at modest significance, although the diffuse flux is established.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson-goran: documented ties to superconducting-circuit work (WACQT director at Chalmers, colleagues of Delsing and Wilson, co-author with Kockum), flagged as possible grounds for recusal if B012 became the leading candidate.
Olsson-eva: a transmission electron microscopist, field-adjacent to B009 (Rose, Haider, Urban), says she should be treated as non-neutral and would consider recusal from the final decision on it.
Pearce-mark (chair): field proximity to B042 IceCube as an astroparticle physicist, flagged in case recusal is considered there; no conflict for B008.

Kroll-stefan: a research stay in John Hall's laboratory and work in laser spectroscopy and ultrastable-laser stabilisation, in the same technical area as B008, though no tie to Katori or Ye is recorded.
Eriksson-olle: field adjacency to B035 through electronic-structure and 2D-materials theory, disclosed as a bias to discount.
questions_for_round2: For B008, is the lattice clock a distinct invention from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, and what exact citation wording would make that distinction explicit without implying the pending SI second redefinition?

Is the Katori and Ye pairing an adequate attribution given the NIST, PTB, SYRTE and Tokyo contributions and the priority between the magic-wavelength proposal and the first demonstrations, and if not, which concrete addition or alternative do members propose?
Do the members who prefer B035 or B022 accept B008 as the lead, and if not, what specific evidence on maturity (B035) or on the Blatt allocation and the 2012 overlap (B022) would change positions?

Should the committee consider a two-part prize, and if so which pairing of B008 with another shortlisted entry would any member support, given that Kroll reports finding none stronger than the clock alone?
For members with disclosed proximity (Johansson on B012, Olsson on B009, Kroll and Pearce on B008 and B042), should any recusal or discount be applied before the final ballot?
summary.chair_observation: The eight statements show a clear plurality for B008 (six of eight explicit preferences, Eriksson and Mehlig placing it first among alternatives), with single-member preferences for B035 and B022. Members who prefer B008 mostly share the same reservations about prior prizes, credit beyond the two names and the SI timing, so round 2 turns on whether those reservations are answered by the citation and not on the underlying science. The chair's own first preference is B008, and this summary does not rule on any candidate.
